metadata.case_name: SZETO YUK v. CHU MING KEUNG AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: fractures of the right collar bone
source: She was treated for fractures of the right collar bone, lower end of the right humerus and of the right pelvis.
the collar bone and pelvis have healed completely.

injuries.description: fracture of the lower end of the right humerus
source: She was treated for fractures of the right collar bone, lower end of the right humerus and of the right pelvis.
the injury to the humerus has severely affected the movement of the elbow joint so that the plaintiff cannot fully straighten her arm and can only bend her elbow to a right angle.
The fractured humerus was treated by way of traction which involved a pin being driven through the forearm.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the elbow or forearm

source: She was treated for fractures of the right collar bone, lower end of the right humerus and of the right pelvis.
the collar bone and pelvis have healed completely.
The pelvic injury was treated by bed rest.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of unspecified pelvic bone without disruption of posterior arch of pelvic ring

injuries.description: fractured the second and third fingers of her right hand
injuries.body_part: second and third fingers of right hand
source: The plaintiff also fractured the second and third fingers of her right hand.
these fingers now cannot be fully straightened or bent into a full grip.
The plaintiff now only has a grip of 10 lbs. with her right hand whereas before the accident, as she is right-handed, she probably had a grip of at least 30 lbs.

manifestations.description: cannot fully straighten her arm and can only bend her elbow to a right angle
these fingers now cannot be fully straightened or bent into a full grip
The plaintiff now only has a grip of 10 lbs. with her right hand whereas before the accident ... probably had a grip of at least 30 lbs.
The plaintiff can no longer use chopsticks as she cannot move her hand closer than 18 inches to her mouth and eats by using a spoon with her left hand.
She cannot use scissors or make other fine movements with her hand so that she is precluded from returning to her previous employment as a sewing and garment worker.
She does her own house work but has some difficulty in washing dishes, clothes and the floor.
The combined effect of the arm and hand injuries is that the plaintiff is left with a 40% permanent disability and a 25% impairment of the whole person.
